output.brief:
The rise is very unlikely to be Tessaly's handling. Since 1 September, Corvane tags printed on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against about 1.5% on the old stock. Pelion, which uses the same handler and crew pool, is unchanged. Corvane transfer tags are also unchanged. The extra bags go to the manual encode desk, wait about 30 minutes, and reach the lateral after it closes. On 14–16 October, counters that used old Brackwater stock read fine (1.6% failures), while kiosks on Fennick failed at 12%. That points to the tag stock, not the handler or the airport scanners. I can't yet say whether the stock is defective or just doesn't suit the printer heat settings, so a defect claim against Fennick is premature.

Next steps:
1. Don't send the breach notice or withhold the fee.
2. Switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater stock now. About five weeks of it is in stores and the contract runs to 31 December.
3. Test the Fennick stock separately, including the printer heat setting.
4. Optionally ask HBAA for an extra encode workstation as a stopgap.

I'm fairly confident (about 85%) in this.
